column3: Close to the Hebrew; “in their dwelling place” renders a rare word of uncertain meaning (perhaps “their swords”).
Close to the Hebrew; “a lawgiver” renders a word for a ruler's staff; “Until Shiloh comes” renders an obscure phrase (also read “until he comes to whom it belongs”), and NKJV capitalizes “Him.”
Close to the Hebrew; “between two burdens” renders a rare word perhaps meaning “sheepfolds” or “saddlebags.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he shall triumph at last” renders “he shall raid at their heels.”
Close to the Hebrew; “a fruitful bough” renders an obscure phrase (literally “son of a fruitful one”), and “branches” renders “daughters.”
Close to the Hebrew; “my ancestors” renders a word that can also be read “ancient mountains,” and “him who was separate” renders “the nazir (consecrated one).”
